messages.subject: questions about read.bismark
parts:
Hi all,

Two questions about this function:
1. does "nolap" parameter will throw away one entire end when the
paired-end overlap at least one base length?

The definition of nolap:
" nolap: if set to TRUE and the SAM file has paired-end reads, the one
read of the overlapping paired-end read pair will be ignored
for methylation calling.
"
Bismark also has a scripts to extract the C site information, for this situation,
the overlaped region will be omitted when call methylation status, but other region that not overlapped will preserve.

2. Can "assembly" parameter be defined to non-model species?
The species I analyzed is not published yet. so this parameter will set to "foo", will this influence the results?

Thank you.

Best,
pch

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: questions about read.bismark
parts:
1. does "nolap" parameter will throw away one entire end when the
paired-end overlap at least one base length?

It is supposed to throw away only the overlapping parts from one read. It shouldn't throw away the whole read unless the whole read is overlapping with the other read pair. This is designed to be similar to what bismark is doing.

2. Can "assembly" parameter be defined to non-model species?
The species I analyzed is not published yet. so this parameter will set to "foo", will this influence the results?

assembly parameter can be any string, it will not effect the downstream analysis provided that you always operate on the same assembly. For example, do not try to merge objects from different assemblies, such as "hg18" and "hg19".
 
Best,
Altuna

Thank you.
